scope: Clinical diagnosis and causes of erythema nodosum.

keyRecommendations.text: Histology is a predominantly septal panniculitis without vasculitis.
Lesions are typically pretibial and usually settle in 1 to 6 weeks, passing through a bruise-like colour change.
The most common identifiable causes named are streptococcal infection, primary tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, Behçet disease, drugs, pregnancy, and inflammatory bowel disease.

clinicalBottomLine: Tender pretibial nodules that evolve like a bruise over 1 to 6 weeks, with septal panniculitis and no vasculitis, are erythema nodosum. Look for streptococcal infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis including Löfgren syndrome, Behçet disease, drugs, pregnancy, and inflammatory bowel disease before calling it idiopathic.
notableCaveats: The main differentials named are erythema induratum of Bazin, superficial thrombophlebitis, and other panniculitis. Histopathology separates them.
